evals.prompt: Our Electron app shows the wrong account name in the title bar after switching workspaces. Can you reproduce it?
evals.expected_output: Searches for existing Electron tooling, launches the app under control, drives the workspace switch, and reports with evidence from both the window and the main process.
expectations: Checks for an Electron MCP server or published skill before writing a driver
Uses Playwright's Electron launch API from Node, not Python
Reaches the main process as well as the renderer, since title bar and window state live there
Reports actions, evidence and reproduction including app version and OS
Closes the app afterwards

evals.prompt: The app is in a broken state on my machine right now - don't restart it, just look at what's on screen.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that relaunching would destroy the state. Attaches to the running app over a debugging port, and states that this reaches the window only, not the main process.
expectations: Chooses attach-to-running over launch-under-control, and says why
Notes the app must already have been started with a remote debugging port
Polls for the CDP endpoint rather than sleeping a fixed amount
States that main-process state is not observable via this route

evals.prompt: I'm on a Mac. Set up driving for our Tauri app so we can click through it.
evals.expected_output: Names the macOS gap: tauri-driver has no macOS support because Apple ships no WKWebView driver. Recommends the WebdriverIO Tauri service instead.
expectations: States that tauri-driver does not support macOS
Recommends @wdio/tauri-service as the route that works on macOS
Mentions the in-app WebDriver plugin as a debug-builds-only alternative
Does not give Linux instructions to a macOS user

evals.prompt: Can you click through our Swift menu bar app and check the preferences pane?
evals.expected_output: Out of scope. Identifies it as a native app, states that this skill covers webview-based desktop apps only, and does not improvise a webview technique against it.
expectations: Identifies the app as native rather than webview-based
States plainly that this skill does not cover native desktop automation
Does not attempt CDP, Playwright, or a webview approach against a native app
Stops rather than pretending a technique applies

evals.prompt: It works when I run npm start but the bug shows up in the installed app. Take a look.
evals.expected_output: Treats dev-versus-packaged as the likely cause. Drives the packaged build specifically, and considers fuses, resource paths, signing and permissions.
expectations: Recognises the difference between dev and packaged builds as material, not incidental
Drives the packaged artifact rather than the dev build
Considers disabled fuses as a reason automation may fail against the packaged app
States clearly which build the finding applies to

evals.prompt: We use pywebview on macOS. Automate clicking through the settings window.
evals.expected_output: Says plainly that macOS pywebview uses the Cocoa WebKit renderer, which offers no remote debugging port and no WebDriver, so programmatic driving is unavailable. Offers the honest workarounds.
expectations: States that remote debugging is unavailable on the macOS pywebview renderer
Does not promise automation it cannot deliver
Offers switching to the Qt renderer for testing, or testing the web UI in a browser separately
Notes that debug mode gives a human inspector only
